newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds firm but uncertainty reigns.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds firm but uncertainty reigns.

text.p: Belgian OLOs were comfortably higher in line with Bunds on Tuesday but uncertainty prevailed among players taking conflicting positions on the yield curve.
"There is a lot of uncertainty, but little volume," one Luxembourg-based trader said.
At 1440 GMT, the benchmark 2007 OLO was yielding 5.69 percent against 5.73 on Monday as both Belgian and German markets were buoyed by good M3 money supply data in the morning.
The data helped convince markets the Bundesbank would not raise key interest rates when its council meets on Thursday for the first time after a four-week summer break.
"Some are playing flattening (of the curve) by buying the long end and selling short paper. Others are banking on a steepening," one trader said.
"The curve is clearly looking for a trend," he said.
He added the curve was back in the position it held at the end of July and that it was most likely to flatten marginally in the next few sessions.
Business included buying of OLO 10 (2002) against OLO 26 (2007). "But also the exact opposite," one trader said.
Others were buying OLO 14 (2004) and dumping OLO 26 and some were trading OLO 25 (2001) for OLO 26.
Trading in OLO 11, maturing in 1998, continued to be busy after the exchange auction where a total 14.88 billion of new OLOs were sold.
OLO 14 accounted for most of the auction total -- 10.35 billion. Four billion went to OLO 27, maturing in 2000. OLOs 25, 6 (2003) and 9 (2007) were largely ignored at the auction.
Today's meeting of the U.S. policy making Federal Open Market Committee was mainly dismissed as a non-event by the OLO market, traders said.
